sections.h2: What does a quitclaim deed do in Arkansas?
sections.html:
A quitclaim deed transfers whatever interest the signer has in the property and makes no promise that the interest is good. It does not clear a mortgage, a tax lien or a co-owner's share, so it works best between people who already trust the title.

Arkansas law treats the paper itself with care. A conveyance has to be acknowledged, the county recorder must accept the format, and a married owner's homestead brings the spouse into the signing. Each of those steps is spelled out in the sections below, with the statute behind it.

sections.h2: What must a deed look like for the recorder to accept it?
sections.html:
The recorder can refuse a deed that fails the format rules in Ark. Code 14-15-402. Missing a margin is the sort of slip that gets a deed sent back.

  • Paper size is 8.5 by 11 inches.
  • The first page needs 2.5 inches of blank space at the top right for the file mark.
  • Sides and bottom need 0.5 inch, and the last page needs 2.5 inches at the bottom.
  • The document carries its title and the names of grantor and grantee.
  • It must be legible and acknowledged under 16-47-207.

The recorder may waive the format for good cause. Documents signed before January 1, 2004, and plats and surveys, are exempt from the format rules.

A separate rule, 14-15-403, requires the preparer's name and address on the first page of an instrument that affects title. A recorder who accepts a noncompliant instrument must refund the fee on request within six months, and the instrument still gives notice. Wills, court decrees and instruments signed before August 1, 1959 are exempt.

sections.h2: Does a spouse have to sign a quitclaim on a homestead?
sections.html:
Yes, when the property is the homestead of a married person, the spouse must join in the deed or sign a separate deed and acknowledge it. Ark. Code 18-12-403 says an instrument affecting a married person's homestead has no validity without that participation.

The exceptions are taxes, laborers' and mechanics' liens, and purchase money. Under 18-12-202, a married person may acknowledge a conveyance of their own property, or release dower, curtesy or homestead in a spouse's property, as if unmarried, with no separate examination.

A quitclaim signed by one spouse alone can leave a gap in the title. If the house was a homestead, ask the title company whether the other spouse's signature is needed.

sections.h2: What if the acknowledgment has a mistake?
sections.html:
Some acknowledgment defects are cured once the deed is recorded, but the cure should not be treated as a plan. Section 18-12-208 lists defects that do not defeat a recorded instrument.

  • A missing or wrong notary seal, for deeds signed after August 13, 1993.
  • A missing or wrong commission expiration date.
  • A wrong date or a missing county.
  • A notary who moved out of the commissioning county.
  • Wording that departs from the statutory form but makes a good-faith attempt at material compliance.

A defective but recorded deed still gives constructive notice of its contents. For instruments recorded on or after April 8, 2013, a proper jurat can substitute for an acknowledgment certificate.

sections.h2: What does recording and transfer tax cost?
sections.html:
Recording fees are set by statute and charged by the circuit clerk, who serves as recorder. Pulaski County's published schedule shows $15 for the first page of a deed and $5 for each added page, under Ark. Code 21-6-306. Other counties post their own schedules, so ask the clerk where the land sits.

ItemAmountSource
Deed, first page (Pulaski County)$15.00Pulaski County Clerk fee schedule
Each added page$5.00Pulaski County Clerk fee schedule
Document non-compliance fee$25.00 per document, plus page feesPulaski County Clerk fee schedule
State transfer tax, base$1.10 per $1,000Ark. Code 26-60-105(a)
State transfer tax, added$2.20 per $1,000, paid by purchaserArk. Code 26-60-105(b)

The two tax pieces add to $3.30 per $1,000 of consideration, and the tax applies only when consideration is over $100, according to the state revenue division. The Miscellaneous Tax Section sells the transfer stamps and can be reached at 501-682-7187.

sections.h2: Which quitclaim deeds are exempt from the transfer tax?
sections.html:
Several transfers are exempt, and a family quitclaim may fall under one of them. Section 26-60-102 lists twelve categories, including these.

  • Property divided between divorcing parties.
  • Instruments given only to secure a debt, and certain transfers to a secured party enforcing a security interest.
  • Corrections of a recorded instrument when tax was already paid.
  • Land sold for delinquent taxes.
  • Beneficiary deeds under 18-12-608.
  • Transfers to or from governments, and some business entity reorganizations.

A FHA, VA or USDA Rural Development home is exempt if the price is $60,000 or less and the seller files a sworn statement that the buyer and spouse have owned no home in the prior three years. A gift between relatives does not appear among the categories, so confirm with the state revenue office before assuming an exemption.

sections.h2: Is a beneficiary deed a better tool than a quitclaim?
sections.html:
For passing a house at death, a beneficiary deed can be the cleaner choice, because it does nothing until the owner dies. Ark. Code 18-12-608 sets the terms: it must say it is not effective until death, and it is valid only if recorded with the county recorder before the owner dies.

  • The owner can revoke it at any time by a signed, recorded revocation. A will cannot revoke it.
  • If several deeds exist, the last one signed before death controls, whatever the recording order.
  • The transfer remains subject to mortgages, liens and leases that exist at death.
  • For joint tenants or spouses holding by the entirety, the deed must be signed by all surviving owners.

The deed is also exempt from the transfer tax. A quitclaim to a child during life hands over a present interest, so speak with a lawyer before choosing between the two.

sections.h2: What is a sensible order of steps for a quitclaim?
sections.html:
Work through the checks in the order the statutes create them, so the recorder has nothing to reject.

  • Confirm every owner and whether the house is a married person's homestead.
  • Put the preparer's name and address on the first page, and leave the file-mark space at the top right.
  • Sign before a notary, with the acknowledgment naming the state and county.
  • Check whether the transfer falls under an exemption, and buy transfer stamps if it does not.
  • Record the deed with the county recorder where the property is located, and keep the receipt.

sections.h2: When does a quitclaim get in the way of selling?
sections.html:
A quitclaim can slow a sale if the buyer's title company questions the gap it creates. Common trouble spots are a missing spouse signature, a mortgage still in the old owner's name, and unpaid property tax.

The tax lien binds the house and ranks ahead of other liens, per 26-34-101, so a deed between family does not move the tax debt away. Cash Home Buyers makes as-is offers on Arkansas houses, including houses where a quitclaim was recorded. If a quitclaim is already recorded on your house, have the recorded copy and any mortgage statement ready when you call.

faqs.q: Does a quitclaim deed guarantee clear title?
faqs.a: No. It passes only the interest the signer holds and makes no promise about liens, co-owners or defects. A mortgage or tax lien stays on the property after a quitclaim.

faqs.q: Does my spouse have to sign if I quitclaim our home?
faqs.a: Yes, if it is your homestead. Section 18-12-403 makes a homestead instrument invalid unless the spouse joins or signs a separate acknowledged deed, with exceptions for taxes, certain liens and purchase money.

faqs.q: How much does it cost to record a deed in Arkansas?
faqs.a: Pulaski County charges $15 for the first page and $5 for each additional page. Other counties publish their own schedules, so check with the circuit clerk in the county where the land is.

faqs.q: What is the Arkansas real estate transfer tax rate?
faqs.a: It is $3.30 per $1,000 of consideration on transfers above $100: $1.10 base plus $2.20 paid by the purchaser. Divorce divisions, security deeds and beneficiary deeds are among the exemptions.

faqs.q: Can I use a quitclaim to transfer a house to my child at death?
faqs.a: A beneficiary deed under 18-12-608 is built for that. It must state it takes effect at death and be recorded before the owner dies.

faqs.q: What if the recorder rejects my deed?
faqs.a: The format rules in 14-15-402 and the preparer statement in 14-15-403 are the usual causes. Fix the margins, names or preparer information and resubmit, or ask the recorder about a good-cause waiver, which may carry a $25 fee.
